scope: Bookworm system CPython and Expat in existing Kuma and Gathio images

sources.authentication: Debian signed APT index and source checksums, downloaded using the isolated review.sources; the DSC signature is not independently verified
sources.reason: CVE-2026-7210: both pyexpat and ElementTree must provide 128-bit salt to Expat >=2.8
sources.patchExtent: The four C/header edits are byte-identical to upstream additions/deletions. Debian context was refreshed without fuzz. All existing Debian patches remain.

sources.authentication: Debian signed APT index and source checksums
sources.architecture: Rebuilt with Bookworm dependencies; not a sid binary, distro migration or glibc replacement
sources.reason: Supply the supported XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes interface and current native parser fixes

build.network: APT preparation only; compiler network disconnected before source build and tests
build.identity: Native package builds run as uid/gid 65534 in disposable storage
build.tests: Explicit upstream Expat suite and 10 Python modules. Full Debian Python test suite is not claimed; nopgo/nolto/nocheck packaging options are used.

staging.entryPoint: node stage.mjs kuma|gathio followed by node app-checks.mjs kuma|gathio
staging.ancestry: Exact current live image and ref must match specs.json; reconcile dependencies before staging
staging.preservation: No other package version, app/config bytes, unrelated library or image configuration changes; retain every existing Expat export
staging.nativeProof: Disposable LD_PRELOAD probe proves both actual parser paths call XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes; it emits counters, never entropy, and is not installed in candidates
staging.services: Kuma synthetic setup/login and PyJWT/Apprise; Gathio native barman imports, DocumentDB/PostGIS typed data, permissions, projection, upstream malformed FlatGeobuf tests and logical restore
staging.testIsolation: No network outside loopback, no production volumes, no notifications; temporary synthetic state removed

sdkCompatibility.finding: The earlier urllib32.8 overlay left Gathio's boto3 1.26.27 / botocore1.29.27 unable to import DEFAULT_CIPHERS. Reproduced on the pre-Python live image and candidate. Barman --help alone missed this deferred provider import; no actual failed user backup is inferred.
sdkCompatibility.repair: Preserve Barman3.20.1 and upgrade exactly three signed Debian architecture-all packages: boto3/botocore1.40.72, s3transfer0.14.0. They support Python3.11 and urllib3<3; no native library or distro transition.
sdkCompatibility.acquisition: node acquire-sdk.mjs; SDK versions and authenticated archive checksums in sdk-packages.json
sdkCompatibility.tests: sdk-native.py: loopback-only TLS S3 fixture, independent SigV4 HMAC verification, environment credentials, wrong-key403 and untrusted-certificate denial, native Barman upload/list/read/download, missing object and synthetic deletion. Twelve tiny requests; no cloud endpoint, actual credential or production backup used.
sdkCompatibility.limits: Not a multipart or real-cloud backup/restore test. All application bytes except the explicit SDK directories remain unchanged.

otherFinding.evidence: The exact Debian tarfile payload lacks the extraction-filter implementation; filter='data' is rejected. Recorded per live image and source SHA by tar-component-proof.mjs, then rechecked in candidates.
otherFinding.limitation: This is not a claim that unrestricted tar extraction is safe and not an exemption for other tar vulnerabilities. Security ledger decisions remain with the release owner.

release.owner: Parent-authorized exact native release only. release.mjs prepare|apply kuma|gathio reuses the standard releaseGroup and rollback gates; only the relevant current image scalar changes.
release.rollback: Restore the exact previously recorded image ref/ID using the normal release procedure; no schema or persistent data migration is introduced
release.retirement: Do not replace these images with vendor tags until the protected-update process verifies equivalent upstream fixes and repeats native checks
release.review: node review.mjs prepares separate expiring mitigation-review.json and not-affected-review.json from fresh scan evidence and byte-checked installed payloads. It never changes the security decision ledger.
